Operating Manual

Step-by-step procedures for the Alora website, on the office Windows computer. Start of Care, documents, scheduling, monitoring, billing readiness and daily checks.

What this manual is based on
  • Alora: public product information, used only to name features. Zenith's live Alora account was not available when this edition was written.
  • Medicare and HIPAA: the Medicare Conditions of Participation for home health agencies (42 CFR 484), the face-to-face requirement (42 CFR 424.22), Medicare payment rules for the Notice of Admission, and the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR 164.312).
  • Florida: section 415.1034, Florida Statutes (reporting of abuse, neglect and exploitation of vulnerable adults).
  • Zenith: the earlier Zenith Alora guide and its standards. Zenith standards here are drafts until approved.

Tab 1 · Start HereHow to use this binder

How to use this binder

Sit at the office computer with the binder open beside the keyboard. Do one procedure at a time. Never do a step from memory.

The method

SEE ITmatch the picture to your screen›
CLICK ITfollow the red numbers in order›
ENTER ITtype only what the page asks›
SAVE ITclick once, then wait›
VERIFY ITcheck the result on screen

Every procedure has the same pattern

  1. Start page. What the procedure is for, what you need before you begin, and the list of steps with page numbers.
  2. Step pages. One picture with red numbers, and the words for what to do after each click. Follow the numbers in order.
  3. Finish page. The final verification checklist, the stop rules, and the things you must not do.

WeekDo these procedures with a trainerThen do them alone

Tab 1 · Start HereHow to read a step page

How to read a step page

Every step page has the same parts in the same places. Learn them once.

A Step number and title
B The picture. A training mockup of the screen. 1 2 3 The red numbers show where to click, in order. Each number has a short label. Follow them in order.
C Do these in order. One line for each red number.
D ENTER: what to type. CHECK: what to check before you save. EXPECTED RESULT: what should happen.
E What you should see
F Do not do this
G If it does not look right: stop
H Alora action what to do in Alora
I Zenith standard Zenith's own rule
J Live Alora check. The Administrator initials this when the picture was compared with live Alora.

The tags

TagWhat it means for you
VERIFY IN LIVE ALORANothing public confirms this name or place. Compare the picture with your screen. If they differ, write the real name in the margin and tell the Administrator.
ALORA FEATUREAlora publicly describes this feature by name. The exact words of the menu or button and their place still have to be checked.
VERIFIEDThe Administrator confirmed the name and place in live Alora. (None yet in this edition.)
FROM LIVE ALORAThe picture is a real screenshot from Zenith's Alora with numbers added.
WINDOWSA standard Windows window, such as the file chooser. Not Alora.
ZENITH FORMA paper form from Tab 11. Not a screen.
Alora actionWhat you do in Alora: click, type, choose, save.
Zenith standardA rule Zenith sets for its own office. It is stricter than, or additional to, what Alora does.
FEDERAL RULEA rule from Medicare, HIPAA or Florida law. The Administrator explains it if you ask.

Tab 1 · Start HereWhat is verified and what is not

What is verified and what is not

Read this page before you trust any picture in this manual.

Plain statement

In this edition, no screen, button, menu or box name has been verified against Zenith's live Alora account. Alora's own training screens are not public and were not available. The pictures are a neutral, clearly labeled wireframe of a web application. They show where on a typical screen an item would be, and they show the order of the clicks. They do not show what Alora really looks like.

Kind of itemStatus in this editionWhat the manual does
Names of Alora features (for example Live Monitor, QA, NOA widget)FEATUREUses the public feature name. Tags the exact menu or button text as 'to verify'.
Menu, button, box and column namesVERIFYDescribes the item in plain words. Tags it. Never presents a guessed name as real.
Order of the clicksVERIFYFollows how web scheduling and records systems normally work. The Administrator confirms it in live Alora.
Windows windows (file chooser, folders, lock screen)WINDOWSStandard Windows behavior.
Paper forms and Zenith rulesZENITHWritten by Zenith. Drafts until the Administrator approves them.

How to close the gap

  1. Live Alora check (about 2 hours). The Administrator works through the Live Alora Verification Worksheet (Tab 11) at a computer signed in to live Alora, and writes the real names and places.
  2. Reissue. The real names go into the manual. Tags change to VERIFIED. Wording that needs changing is changed.
  3. Real screenshots (optional but best). Capture each screen from live Alora, add the red numbers with the annotation tool, and drop the file into the manual. The picture then says FROM LIVE ALORA.
  4. Approve. The Administrator signs the Document control page.

Features Alora documents publicly

Alora's public product information names these features. That tells us a feature exists, not where it is on Zenith's screens.

  • Dashboard
  • Pending 485 forms, orders and OASIS shown in one place
  • NOA dashboard widget for timely filing
  • Scheduling
  • QA
  • Billing
  • HR functions
  • Messaging
  • Paperless records (scanned document storage)
  • Patient communication log
  • Insurance records (unlimited per patient)
  • Physician lookup from the NPI registry
  • Intake and referral tracking
  • Live Monitor
  • Custom Documents
  • Schedule views by patient, caregiver or agency
  • Schedule views by day, week, month or certification period
  • Batch entry scheduling
  • Conflict and compliance alerts (authorization, visit frequency)
  • Color-coded delay and no-show warnings
  • Visits held for manual review before they are sent
  • OASIS with scrubber
  • Plan of care (CMS-485)
  • Billing for all payers
  • One-click NOA generation
  • Built-in electronic faxing

Tab 1 · Start HereWho does what

Who does what

Office staff prepare, check and report. Clinicians and the DON decide clinical questions. The Administrator decides everything else that this manual says needs approval.

RoleWhat they do in this manualWhat they never do
Intake staffLog and check referral packets. Find patients. Scan, name and upload documents. Check demographics. Check orders and face-to-face papers.Accept or decline a referral. Change clinical information. Choose the nurse.
Second personVerifies orders and face-to-face documents that someone else uploaded.Verify their own upload.
SchedulerAdds visits from a signed request. Checks the calendar. Changes a visit only with written approval. Tells team members and patients.Change the ordered frequency. Choose the nurse for a start of care.
Office staff on dutyWatch the Live Monitor. Call about late visits. Gather facts for exceptions. Do the daily checks.Change a visit status or time. Approve an exception.
QA reviewer (named by the DON)Judges clinical content. Returns items for correction.Approve their own work.
Billing staffCheck billing readiness. Create and send the NOA when named by the Administrator. Send claims.Change clinical documents.
Director of Nursing (DON)Decides referrals and clinical questions. Names the nurse for every start of care. Approves clinical changes.
AdministratorOwns this manual. Approves record changes, document removals, EVV exceptions, user logins and anything marked 'Administrator'.
Your name in this binder

Write who fills each role at Zenith, so a new employee knows whom to ask.

Tab 1 · Start HereWhen to stop and ask

When to stop and ask

These rules apply to every procedure. Each procedure also has its own stop rules on its finish page. To stop is always correct. A guess that goes wrong is not.

Always stop and ask the Administrator or DON if
  • A screen or a button does not look like the picture and you are not sure what to click.
  • The patient's name or date of birth does not match a document.
  • Two patients could be the right one, or no patient can be found after three searches.
  • A document is in the wrong patient's chart. Tell the Administrator now.
  • An error message appears, or Alora does nothing after you click.
  • An alert appears while you schedule or save.
  • The 48-hour deadline cannot be met, or an NOA is close to its 5-day limit.
  • An order or face-to-face document is missing, unsigned or outside its date window.
  • Someone asks you to change a time, a status or a record to make it look right.
  • Someone asks for patient information and you are not sure they may have it.
  • You think someone used your login, or you used someone else's.
  • You are asked to do something this manual says needs approval.

What to say

Say it in short, plain sentences. You do not have to use perfect English. Use this pattern:

1. "I am **stopping** at procedure      , step      ."
2. "I saw               ."
3. "I have **not changed** anything."
4. "What should I do?"

Do
  • Stop at once.
  • Leave the screen as it is.
  • Write the time and the words you saw.
  • Ask.
Do not
  • Do not try a different button to see what happens.
  • Do not start again and hope it fixes itself.
  • Do not hide a mistake.

Zenith standards in this manual (1 of 2)

These are the times, numbers and rules that Zenith sets for its own office. They are drafts. The Administrator initials each one to approve it, or writes a change. Where a federal rule also applies, it is shown. A Zenith standard must never allow more time than the law allows.

No.StandardWhereFederal rule it must not exceedApproved (initials)
1Log every referral packet within 15 minutes of arrival.P6The 48-hour initial visit clock starts at referral.
2The DON or Administrator decides every referral. Office staff never accept, hold or decline.P6, P27
3Identify a patient with two identifiers: name and date of birth.P3, P4, P8
4Search three ways before creating a patient. Create only after the DON accepts.P5B
5Name files LASTNAME_​FIRSTNAME_​DOCUMENTTYPE_​YYYYMMDD.pdf. Scan as PDF at 300 dpi, one patient and one document type per file.P9
6Verify a document in the same session you upload it. Orders and face-to-face: a second person verifies.P8, P10
7Every new order goes to the DON the same day, signed or not.P11
8Tell the DON the same day about a face-to-face problem.P12Face-to-face visit 90 days before to 30 days after start of care (42 CFR 424.22).
9The first nurse visit is scheduled inside 48 hours of the referral, unless the physician ordered a later date.P13Initial assessment within 48 hours (42 CFR 484.55).
10Visits follow a signed Visit Scheduling Request. Office staff never change the frequency.P14Visits follow the plan of care.

Purpose

Patient information is private. This procedure shows the three habits that protect it at the office computer: lock it, log out, and keep files and paper safe.

Before you start

  • You are working at a Zenith office computer.

Who and how long

Who: Every office employee, every day.

Time: 1 minute each time.

Steps in this procedure

  1. 1Lock the computer when you leave your seatp. 29
  2. 2Log out of Alora at the end of the dayp. 30
  3. 3Keep scanned files and paper safep. 31

Tab 2 · Sign In and NavigateHIPAA Precautions at the Office Computer

HIPAA precautions at the office computer

Read this page before your first day. Keep it in the binder.

Always
  • Use only your own login.
  • Lock the computer when you leave (Windows key + L).
  • Open only the patients you need for your job.
  • Check the patient name and birth date before you save anything.
  • Put papers away and close the scan folder.
  • Report a problem the same minute you notice it.
Never
  • Share a password or let someone work under your login.
  • Take photos or screenshots of patient information on a personal phone.
  • Send patient information by personal email, text or social media.
  • Leave a patient screen open where visitors can read it.
  • Look at a record out of curiosity (family, friends, neighbors).
  • Discuss a patient where others can hear.

What counts as patient information

Any information that can point to one patient and relates to health or care: name, address, phone, birth date, insurance number, diagnosis, medicines, photos, orders, notes and scanned documents. If it can identify one patient, treat it as private.

If something goes wrong

  1. Stop what you are doing.
  2. Tell the Administrator right away. Do not wait until the end of the day.
  3. Say what happened, when, and which patient. Do not guess and do not hide anything.
  4. Follow the Administrator's instructions.
Federal rule

HIPAA requires each person to have a unique login, requires safeguards for patient information, and lets Zenith check who opened or changed a record. Act as if every click is recorded.

Before you start

  • The referral, face sheet and insurance card copy.
  • The Administrator's or DON's OK to admit (Zenith standard).
  • The New Patient Check form (Tab 11). Write your three searches on it.
Who and how long

Who: Trained intake staff only.

Time: 10 minutes.

A referral is the request that starts care. This procedure shows how to log it the moment it arrives, check that the packet is complete, record it in Alora, and hand it to the DON for the decision. It protects the 48-hour clock.

Before you start

  • The referral packet (fax, e-fax, email or hand delivered).
  • The SOC Packet Intake Log and Referral Review forms (Tab 11).
  • A pen. The clock or the fax time stamp.
Who and how long

Who: Intake staff.

Time: 15 minutes.

Steps in this procedure

  1. 1Write down when the packet arrivedp. 60
  2. 2Sort the packet and check what is therep. 61
  3. 3Review the referral for the basicsp. 62
  4. 4Find the patient in Alorap. 63
  5. 5Record the referral in Alorap. 64
  6. 6Give the packet to the DON for the decisionp. 65

Tab 5 · Start of Care (SOC) WorkflowThe SOC clocks

The SOC clocks

Five time limits start when a referral arrives or care starts. Missing one can delay care or reduce payment. Write the dates on the SOC Desk Checklist the day the packet arrives.

ClockStartsDueWho watches
First nurse visit (initial assessment)The referral arrives, or the patient returns homeWithin 48 hours, or on the start of care date the physician orderedIntake, then the DON
Face-to-face visit (paper)Start of care dateThe visit happened 90 days before to 30 days after the start of careIntake staff, then the DON
Comprehensive assessment (OASIS)Start of care dateFinished within 5 calendar days after the start of careThe assessing nurse, then the DON
OASIS sentThe day the assessment is finishedSent within 30 daysQA
NOA (Notice of Admission)Start of care dateSent within 5 calendar days of the start of care. Late NOAs reduce payment for each late day.Billing
How to use this page
  • On the day a referral arrives, write the 48-hour deadline at the top of the SOC Desk Checklist (Tab 11).
  • When the SOC visit is scheduled, write the NOA due date (SOC date plus 5 calendar days).
  • Count calendar days, not business days. Weekends and holidays count.
  • The Administrator confirms these rules each year. If this page and the Administrator disagree, follow the Administrator.
Federal rule

These clocks come from the Medicare Conditions of Participation for home health agencies and the Medicare home health payment rules. The initial assessment visit is due within 48 hours of the referral (or of the patient's return home), or on the start of care date ordered by the physician. The comprehensive assessment is due within 5 calendar days after the start of care.

Stop and ask the Administrator or DON if
  • A clock will be missed or is already missed.
  • The physician wants a start date that is later than 48 hours.
  • The patient asks to start later.
  • You are not sure which date to count from.

Tab 5 · Start of Care (SOC) WorkflowP7U · SOC Document UploadStart
Tab 5 · Procedure P7U

SOC Document Upload

Purpose

To put the three documents of a Start of Care packet into the correct patient's chart in Alora, each under its own document type, and to prove they are there. The three documents are the referral, the physician order and the face-to-face documentation. Alora documents scanned-document storage for patients; every button name here must be verified in live Alora.

Before you start

  • The three files are scanned, named and checked, and waiting in Ready to upload (P9): referral, order, face-to-face.
  • The packet paper. The patient's name and date of birth.
  • You are signed in (P1).
Who and how long

Who: Trained intake staff. A second person verifies orders and face-to-face.

Time: About 20 minutes for all three documents.

Steps in this procedure

  1. 1AFind the correct patientp. 124
  2. 1BOpen the record and confirm who it isp. 125
  3. 2Open the patient's document areap. 126
  4. 3AReferral: click Add, then Choose filep. 127
  5. 3BReferral: pick the file in the Windows windowp. 128
  6. 3CReferral: choose the type, check, and Savep. 129
  7. 4Physician order: add, choose, type, date, Savep. 130
  8. 5Face-to-face: add, choose, type, date, Savep. 131
  9. 6AVerify: the completed document listp. 132
  10. 6BVerify: open each documentp. 133
SEE ITmatch the picture›
CLICK ITfollow the red numbers›
ENTER ITtype only what is asked›
SAVE ITone click, then wait›
VERIFY ITcheck the result

Tab 5 · Procedure P13

Prepare and Schedule the SOC Visit

Purpose

Stage 10 of the SOC workflow. Before anyone is scheduled, the office proves the packet is ready, the DON names the nurse, the patient agrees on a time, and then the start of care visit is put on the Alora schedule and checked. The first nurse visit is due within 48 hours of the referral, unless the physician ordered a later date.

Before you start

  • Stages 1 to 9 are initialed on the SOC Desk Checklist.
  • The SOC Readiness Check, SOC Assignment and SOC Call Notes forms (Tab 11).
  • The referral arrival time, and the DON or Administrator's accepted decision.
Who and how long

Who: Scheduler. The DON names the nurse.

Time: 15 to 25 minutes.

Steps in this procedure

  1. 1Check that the patient is readyp. 136
  2. 2Get the nurse from the DONp. 137
  3. 3Call the patient and agree a timep. 138
  4. 4Add the SOC visit in Alorap. 139
  5. 5Read the alerts, then Savep. 140
  6. 6Check the visit is on the calendarp. 141
  7. 7Close out: checklist, NOA date, tell the nursep. 142

Tab 6 · Procedure P14

Schedule Visits

Purpose

To put a visit on the Alora schedule correctly: the right patient, the right discipline, the right team member, the right day and time, and the right repeat pattern. The example in this procedure is a weekly home health aide visit. A start of care visit uses the same screens (P13).

Before you start

  • A Visit Scheduling Request signed by the DON (Tab 11). It shows the discipline, how often, the first visit date and the team member.
  • The patient's agreed times (from your call).
  • You are signed in (P1).
Who and how long

Who: Schedulers.

Time: 5 to 10 minutes for each patient.

Steps in this procedure

  1. 1Get the DON's requestp. 146
  2. 2Open the Schedulep. 147
  3. 3Start a new visitp. 148
  4. 4Choose who and whatp. 149
  5. 5Choose when and how oftenp. 150
  6. 6Read the alerts, then Savep. 151
  7. 7Check the new visits on the calendarp. 152
  8. 8Tell the team member and the patientp. 153

Tab 6 · Procedure P16

Change a Schedule When Authorized

Purpose

To move or reassign a visit only when the DON or the Administrator has approved it in writing, and to make sure the patient and the team member both know. A careless change can cause a missed visit, a late start of care or a billing problem.

Before you start

  • A Schedule Change Approval form signed by the DON or the Administrator (Tab 11).
  • The Change Notice Log (Tab 11).
  • The patient's and team member's phone numbers.
Who and how long

Who: Schedulers. Only with written approval.

Time: 10 minutes.

Steps in this procedure

  1. 1Get the written approval firstp. 164
  2. 2Find the visit on the calendarp. 165
  3. 3Open the visit and change only what was approvedp. 166
  4. 4Write the reason and Savep. 167
  5. 5Check the resultp. 168
  6. 6Tell the patient and the team memberp. 169

Monitor Visits (Live Monitor)

Purpose

To watch visits as they happen, so a late or missed visit is found in minutes and not the next day. Alora documents a Live Monitor with color-coded warnings for delays and no-shows. Office staff watch, call and report. They never change a visit status.

Before you start

  • You are signed in (P1).
  • The Late or Missed Visit Log (Tab 11).
  • The phone numbers of team members on duty.
Who and how long

Who: Office staff on duty.

Time: 5 minutes each time. Check at the start of the day, at midday and near the end.

Steps in this procedure

  2. 2Read the statusesp. 174

Who and how long

Tab 8 · Procedure P22

NOA Workflow (Notice of Admission)

Purpose

The NOA tells Medicare that a patient has started care. It must be sent within 5 calendar days of the start of care. If it is late, payment is reduced for each late day. Alora documents an NOA dashboard widget and one-click NOA generation. Only staff the Administrator has named click the create button.

Before you start

  • The start of care date for the patient.
  • The NOA Check and the NOA Tracking Log (Tab 11).
  • You are signed in (P1).
  • Ask the Administrator if you are allowed to create and send NOAs.
Who and how long

Who: Billing staff. Other office staff prepare and watch.

Time: 10 minutes for each NOA, plus a daily look until accepted.

Steps in this procedure

  1. 1Find NOAs that are duep. 208
  2. 2Open the NOA listp. 209
  3. 3Check the patient before creating the NOAp. 210
  4. 4Create and send the NOAp. 211
  5. 5Check that it was acceptedp. 212
  6. 6Write it on the tracking logp. 213

Signing in, screens and saving. Find what you see in the left column. If the last column says STOP, stop and ask the Administrator. Write the time and what you saw on the Problem Report (Tab 11).

Tab 10 · Problems and ApprovalsA document is in the wrong chart: the first ten minutes

A document is in the wrong chart

This is the one mistake that must be reported at once. It is a privacy problem and it can also cause a wrong care decision. Do these five things, in this order.

The first ten minutes
  1. Stop. Do not click anything else in that chart.
  2. Do not delete, move or rename the document. The Administrator decides how to correct it.
  3. Write down: the name of the patient whose chart has the document, the name of the patient it belongs to, the document name, the date and the time.
  4. Tell the Administrator now. Go to the Administrator's desk or call. Do not send an email or a text with patient names.
  5. Close the chart and wait for instructions.
Do
  • Tell the truth about what happened.
  • Tell the Administrator even if you are not sure.
  • Write what you did and when.
Do not
  • Do not try to fix it quietly.
  • Do not tell anyone outside Zenith.
  • Do not wait until the end of the day.

Write it here

Patient whose chart has the document:

Patient it belongs to:

Document, date and time:

Time the Administrator was told:

Federal rule

HIPAA requires Zenith to look into any use or disclosure of patient information that is not allowed, and to decide whether it must be reported. That decision belongs to the Administrator and the privacy contact, not to office staff.

Quick Card 1 of 6 · Keep beside the computer

How to Find a Patient

  1. Sign in to Alora (your own login). Click Patients in the main menu.
  2. Click the search box. Type the last name.
  3. If there is a date of birth box, type the birth date.
  4. Click Search.
  5. Read every row: name, date of birth, record number.
  6. Match two things: the name AND the date of birth.
  7. One match: click that row to open the record.
  8. Read the banner name before you do anything else.
Stop and ask the Administrator or DON if
  • Two patients match.
  • No patient matches after three searches.
  • The status is not what you expected.
Do not
  • Do not create a patient after one search.
  • Do not open a row because it looks close.
  • Do not keep two patients open.

Full procedure with pictures: p. 35. Button names in your Alora may differ from these words. Write the real names in the margin once the Administrator has verified them.

Quick Card 2 of 6 · Keep beside the computer

How to Upload a Document

  1. Scan: PDF, 300 dpi, one patient, one document type.
  2. Name it: LASTNAME_​FIRSTNAME_​TYPE_​YYYYMMDD.pdf. Save it in Ready to upload.
  3. Open the file. Check the name and the pages.
  4. Find the patient (Card 1). Banner name = file name.
  5. Click the Documents section. Is it already listed? If yes, stop.
  6. Click Add, then Choose file. Pick your file. Click Open.
  7. Choose the document type. Type the document date.
  8. Check patient, file, type, date. Click Save once.
  9. Verify (Card 4).
Stop and ask the Administrator or DON if
  • The banner name is not the file name.
  • No document type matches.
  • An error appears.
  • The document is in the wrong chart: tell the Administrator now.
Do not
  • Do not upload into the wrong chart.
  • Do not click Save twice.
  • Do not delete a document.

Full procedure with pictures: p. 73. Button names in your Alora may differ from these words. Write the real names in the margin once the Administrator has verified them.

Quick Card 3 of 6 · Keep beside the computer

SOC Processing (14 stages)

  1. Receive: write the arrival time.
  2. Review: same name on every page. DON decides.
  3. Find or create the patient (search three ways first).
  4. Open the record. Name and birth date match.
  5. Upload referral, order, face-to-face.
  6. Verify each document opens.
  7. Enter and verify patient information.
  8. Verify orders: signed and dated.
  9. Verify face-to-face: date in the window.
  10. Prepare and schedule the SOC visit. 48-hour limit.
  11. Verify the clinical workflow is in place.
  12. Monitor the visit.
  13. QA: complete and sent on.
  14. Billing: NOA within 5 calendar days.
Stop and ask the Administrator or DON if
  • The 48-hour limit cannot be met.
  • The order or face-to-face is missing or not valid.
  • A document is in the wrong chart.
Do not
  • Do not skip a stage.
  • Do not tick a box you did not do.
  • Do not schedule before the DON names the nurse.

Full procedure with pictures: p. 105. Button names in your Alora may differ from these words. Write the real names in the margin once the Administrator has verified them.

Quick Card 4 of 6 · Keep beside the computer

Document Verification

  1. Open the patient's document list.
  2. Find each document you uploaded. Once each.
  3. Click the document to open it.
  4. Read the patient name and date of birth on the page.
  5. Look at every page. All readable?
  6. Check the type and the document date.
  7. Fill in the Document Verification form. Initial it.
  8. Orders and face-to-face: a second person checks too.
Stop and ask the Administrator or DON if
  • A document is in the wrong chart.
  • A document will not open or cannot be read.
  • You find a duplicate.
  • The type does not match the paper.
Do not
  • Do not delete or rename a document.
  • Do not assume it is fine because the upload finished.
  • Do not remove the scan file before you verify.

Full procedure with pictures: p. 83. Button names in your Alora may differ from these words. Write the real names in the margin once the Administrator has verified them.

Quick Card 5 of 6 · Keep beside the computer

Scheduling a Visit

  1. Get the signed Visit Scheduling Request from the DON.
  2. Click Schedule in the main menu.
  3. Click Add visit.
  4. Choose patient, visit type, team member.
  5. Enter date, time, repeat (same number of visits as the order).
  6. Read every alert.
  7. Click Save once.
  8. Check the calendar: once, right day, right person.
  9. Tell the team member and the patient.
Stop and ask the Administrator or DON if
  • There is no signed request.
  • An alert names a conflict, a missing authorization or a frequency problem.
  • A start of care visit cannot be inside 48 hours.
  • An error appears.
Do not
  • Do not change the ordered frequency.
  • Do not use a team member the DON did not name.
  • Do not click Save twice.

Full procedure with pictures: p. 145. Button names in your Alora may differ from these words. Write the real names in the margin once the Administrator has verified them.

Quick Card 6 of 6 · Keep beside the computer

Daily Office Alora Check

  1. Sign in with your own login.
  2. Read pending items and the NOA box. NOA due today goes to billing.
  3. Check the Live Monitor. Call about every late visit.
  4. Open the exception list. Start a follow-up for each new one.
  5. Look at today's schedule. Every visit has a team member.
  6. Midday: Live Monitor again.
  7. One hour before the end of the day: Live Monitor again.
  8. Check the scan folder: only files still waiting.
  9. Log out. Lock the computer (Windows key + L). Initial the sheet.
Stop and ask the Administrator or DON if
  • An NOA is due today and not sent.
  • A start of care visit is late or missed.
  • An exception is older than 2 business days.
  • A patient file is where it should not be.
Do not
  • Do not skip a step on a busy day.
  • Do not tick a box you did not do.
  • Do not sign in as someone else.

Tab 11 · Forms and Quick CardsLive Alora Verification Worksheet: instructions

Live Alora Verification Worksheet

The pictures in this manual are training mockups. Nobody has checked them against Zenith's live Alora account yet. This worksheet is how that check is done, once, by the Administrator.

How to do the check (about 2 hours, at an office computer, signed in to live Alora)
  1. Sit with the Administrator. Open live Alora. Do not type or save anything in a real patient record.
  2. Go down the worksheet one row at a time. For each row, open the screen named on the pages shown in the third column.
  3. Write the exact words Alora shows for that button, menu or box in the 'Alora says' column. Write where it is (for example 'left menu, third item').
  4. If the row says 'Alora feature documented', the feature exists. You are confirming only the words and the place.
  5. If a row does not exist in your Alora, write NONE and the real way to do the task. Tell the Administrator. That step of the manual must be rewritten.
  6. When a row is correct, initial the last column.
  7. Give the finished worksheet to the person who maintains this manual. They enter the real names and the manual is reissued. Pictures then show 'verified'.
What the two tags mean
  • Verify (dashed gold): nothing public confirms this name or place. Verify it.
  • Alora feature (blue): Alora publicly describes this feature by name (from its website and review sites). The exact menu or button text and its place are still to verify.

There are 83 rows on the next 7 pages. Rows for paper forms and Windows screens are not on this list because they are not Alora screens.

Checked by (Administrator)
Date
Alora version or release date shown on screen (if any)

Tab 11 · Forms and Quick CardsGlossary (1 of 2)

Glossary (1 of 2)

Words used in this manual, in plain language.

Administrator
The person who runs Zenith and approves changes. You stop and ask the Administrator when this manual says so.
Alert
A warning Alora shows, for example a scheduling conflict. Read it. Do not click through it.
Alora
The web system Zenith uses for patient records, scheduling, visit tracking, quality review and billing. Office staff use it in a browser on a Windows computer.
Certification period
Up to 60 days of care covered by one plan of care.
Chart (patient record)
Everything stored about one patient.
Claim
A bill sent to an insurance company or program for care given.
Demographics
Basic facts about a patient: name, birth date, address, phone, language, emergency contact.
Discharge
The end of care for a patient.
Discipline
A kind of care worker: nurse (RN), physical therapist (PT), occupational therapist (OT), speech therapist (ST), aide, social worker (MSW).
DON
Director of Nursing. The nurse leader who decides clinical questions and names the nurse for each start of care.
Document type
The label you choose when you upload a document, for example referral. It helps everyone find the document later.
Duplicate
A second copy of the same patient or the same document. Duplicates cause errors. Report them. Do not delete them.
EVV
Electronic visit verification. Proof from a phone or device that a visit happened: who, where and when.
Exception
A visit record that does not match the plan, for example a missing clock-out.
Face-to-face (F2F)
A visit in which a physician or allowed practitioner saw the patient in person. Medicare requires it for home health.
HIPAA
The federal law that protects the privacy of health information.
Live Monitor
An Alora screen that shows visits as they happen, with warnings for late visits and no-shows.

Tab 11 · Forms and Quick CardsGlossary (2 of 2)

Glossary (2 of 2)

Words used in this manual, in plain language.

MBI
Medicare Beneficiary Identifier. The patient's Medicare number.
NOA
Notice of Admission. It tells Medicare that a patient has started care. It is due within 5 calendar days of the start of care.
NPI
National Provider Identifier. A 10-digit number that identifies a physician or other provider.
OASIS
A standard assessment a nurse or therapist completes at start of care and at other times. Its answers are sent to Medicare.
Payer
The one who pays for care: Medicare, Medicaid or an insurance company.
Physician order
A written instruction from a doctor for the care a patient will receive.
Plan of care (485)
The document that lists a patient's care, goals and how often visits happen. The physician signs it.
Protected health information (PHI)
Any detail that can identify a patient and relates to health or care. Treat everything in Alora as PHI.
QA
Quality assurance. A check that work is complete and correct before it moves on.
Recertification
A new assessment near the end of a 60-day period when care continues.
Referral
A request for Zenith to care for a patient, from a doctor, hospital or family.
Scan
To make a digital copy of a paper.
Start of care (SOC)
The date of the first visit that starts care for a new patient.
Team member
A person who goes to visits: a nurse, therapist or aide.
Upload
To copy a file from the office computer into Alora.
Verify
To prove something is true by checking it yourself.
